div.head: Iudex 9.1
div.ab: Þa unrihtwisan deman hí beoð wyrsan þonne herigende here: here man mæg foroft befleon; ac þa deman for hira anwealde man ne mæg befleon, ðonne he him of hira ceastrewarena forðrycnesse gestreon gaderiað.
Hosticum potest aliquotiens homo fuga uel defensione uitare, prauos iudices non ita potest, quotiens aduersus subditos malis desideriis inflammantur.

Die ungerechten Richter, die sind schlimmer als verheerendes [Feindes]heer: vor einem Heere kann man gar oft flüchten; aber jenen Richtern kann wegen ihrer Amtsgewalt niemand entrinnen, sobald sie aus Erpressung ihrer Bürger sich Gewinn sammeln.

Unjust judges are worse than a ravaging [enemy] army: one can very often flee from an army; but from those judges, because of their official power, no one can escape when they gather gain for themselves by oppressing their citizens.
Unjust judges are worse than a plundering army. A man may often flee from an army, but from the power of judges no man can flee. Then they oppress the townspeople to gain profit.
div.note: U: translator unrecorded: check; Isidore, Sent. III 52.9.

note.seg: Da die Stelle aus Isidor stammt, darf man nicht etwa folgern, jedes Gericht sitze nur in der Stadt; s. d. Gl 12.—Zu gestreon s. o. 9²: strynan
Since the passage comes from Isidor, one must not conclude, say, that every court sat only in the town; see that word in Gl 12.—On gestreon see above 9²: strynan
